transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm visiting because I've had this overwhelming surge of energy and my thoughts are constantly racing. I just can't seem to stop talking or sit still at all. This has been going on for about four weeks now.

During these past four weeks, have you experienced any symptoms so severe that you required hospitalization, or have you noticed a complete loss of touch with reality, such as hearing voices or holding beliefs that others find clearly untrue?

Yes, I've definitely heard voices whispering to me when there's nobody else in the room, and I know for a fact that I'm being monitored because of my special abilities. Everyone else tells me it's not real, but they just don't understand the connection or the power behind it all.
Do you experience these voices or the belief that you are being monitored only when your mood is extremely high or low, or do these experiences persist even when your mood feels relatively stable?

Yes, they definitely persist even when my mood feels completely stable. There have been times, lasting at least a couple of weeks, where I didn't feel particularly high or low, but I still heard the whispering and felt like I was being watched. It doesn't seem to depend on my mood at all.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates were Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features and Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type). Because the patient reports that psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and delusions) persist for at least two weeks in the absence of prominent mood symptoms, the criteria for Schizoaffective Disorder are met, and Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features is ruled out as the psychotic features are not exclusively present during mood episodes.
